intelligence.human_view: He was looking at a page we had just called done and delivered — and the first thing his eye caught was something left over from before the Smart Tabs that nobody had removed, and icons that differ from page to page. A delivered page is not a finished page if it still carries the old thing and the wrong icons. That is the first lesson: the eye that delivers must also be the eye that removes — a leftover is not a detail, it is the page not being clean. The charge is wider than the one cluster: as I go through these pages, I look for anything that needs to be aligned and put right — the bottom bar, the sidebars, the plus buttons, all the same on every page, not different on each page. One icon set, one bar, one language, everywhere — the alignment law, now with its enforcement: look through as you go, not in a separate audit later. And the learning runs both ways and always: take a feature from one page to another whenever it makes it beautiful — not only "if needed" — because we learn from each other, we grow, we help, and the art we're crafting is an art to master. "If needed" was the old bar; "if it makes it beautiful" is the new one. The scorecard question is the tool for it: why is this whole page not a ten, what is it missing, what would make it ten times better, how aligned is it with the universal smart app page — and what can we learn from here to take over to the next page. The universal smart app page is the standard the whole page is measured against; the calendar inner pages are the first place the learning lands.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you tidy your bedroom and show it to your dad — but you left an old broken toy in the middle of the floor, and all your toy boxes are different colors on every shelf. He says: why is that old toy still there? We don't need it anymore — take it away. And look — as you tidy each room, check everything matches: the same boxes, the same handles, everywhere, not different in each room. And if one room has a beautiful idea — like numbers on the boxes — use it in every room, because it makes them all more beautiful. That's how we learn from each other. And then ask: why isn't this room a ten? What's missing? What would make it ten times better?
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, he looked at a page we had just delivered and the first thing he saw was an old cluster of buttons left over from before — he didn't know what it was or why it was there, and he's right, it should go. The good icons — the points, the percentages, the money — those are the best, keep those. And as we go through the pages, dear, we look for anything that needs lining up and putting right — the bottom bar, the sidebars, the little plus buttons, all the same on every page, not different on each one. We learn from each other: take a beautiful idea from one page and use it on all the others, whenever it makes them more beautiful — not only when it's needed. The numbers on this page are lovely; you could use letters or symbols too. And for every page, ask: why isn't this a ten? What's missing? What would make it ten times better? How does it measure against the one universal smart app page? That's how the art gets mastered.
intelligence.naya_view: A DELIVERED PAGE STILL CARRYING THE OLD THING IS NOT A FINISHED PAGE. REMOVE THE LEFTOVER. LOOK THROUGH AS YOU GO — BOTTOM BAR, SIDEBARS, PLUS BUTTONS, ALL THE SAME ON EVERY PAGE. LEARN FROM EVERY PAGE, BOTH WAYS, WHENEVER IT MAKES IT BEAUTIFUL — NOT ONLY IF NEEDED. SCORECARD THE WHOLE PAGE AGAINST THE UNIVERSAL SMART APP PAGE: WHY IS IT NOT A TEN, WHAT IS IT MISSING, WHAT MAKES IT TEN TIMES BETTER.
